content.text:
The landing page is in `src/App.vue`, and `npm run build` passes. I haven't opened it in a browser, so none of the keyboard or screen-reader behaviour has been tried.

- **Title and intro:** an `h1` and a short intro paragraph. A skip link jumps to the sign-up form.
- **Tracks:** three `CabCard`s with `href` set to `/tracks/board`, `/tracks/digital` and `/tracks/larp`. The title is the single link and it stretches over the whole card, so a click anywhere works. There is one tab stop per card.
- **Sign-up form:** name, email and experience level (`CabTextField` and `CabSelect`), plus a `CabCheckbox` for the code of conduct.
  - **Validation:** it only runs when you press Sign up. The submit button is never disabled.
  - **Errors:** a problem shows an inline message and an error summary that takes focus. Unaccepted conduct gives "Accept the code of conduct to sign up." and stops the form submitting.
- **Email reminders:** a `CabSwitch` that applies straight away, with no save button. A polite live region announces "Email reminders turned on. Saved." The "save" is only a stand-in, so nothing is stored or sent yet. Replace the `watch` on `reminders` in `src/App.vue` with a real API call.
- **Confirmation:** a valid submit opens a `CabDialog` listing the name, email and level, with "Go back" and "Confirm booking". Confirming shows a "You're booked in" message. That booking is also only simulated. Nothing is sent anywhere yet.

My first pass guessed some `--cab-*` colour names that don't exist in the tokens. I replaced them with the real ones (`--cab-color-bg-canvas`, `--cab-color-text-default`, `--cab-color-danger-text` and so on) and rebuilt.

`CabCheckbox` has no `error` prop, so the conduct error is plain text under the checkbox rather than linked to it with `aria-describedby`. The error summary does list it.
